extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists, bacterial taxonomists, members of international nomenclature committees
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, committee duties, and procedural standards for the development, interpretation, publication, and administration of bacteriological nomenclature (International Bacteriological Code) including duties of the International Committee and Judicial Commission and related practices (e.g., type culture deposition, conservation of names, prize selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: van Niel Prize: selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The individual receiving this prize will be selected ... as having made the most distinguished contribution in the field of bacterial systematics in the previous four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is for contributions over the previous four-year period; nominations to be solicited by Executive Secretary-Treasurer from member societies; the role of ICSB is strictly advisory; the Head of the Department of Microbiology at the University of Queensland selects upon consultation with a panel of experts nominated on behalf of the ICSB.

rubrics_metrics.name: van Niel Prize: award timing and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Prize to be awarded at each Congress (later adjusted to triennial cycle); prize money derived from income generated from existing capital of the fund and ICSB has no financial obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University of Queensland administers the prize and may provide travel funds to recipient separate from prize money; rules were altered to align award with IUMS Congress scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a single International Committee for bacterial nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: The interests of bacterial nomenclature will best be served by placing the subject in the hands of a single International Committee, adequately representative of all departments of Bacteriology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should be representative of all aspects of bacteriology so that its decisions will carry weight internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee constitution: permanent secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Two permanent secretaries shall be elected: one primarily to represent medical and veterinary bacteriology, the other primarily to represent the other phases of bacteriology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a secretaryship becomes vacant it may be filled pro tempore by the Committee; a permanent secretary should be chosen by action of the next succeeding International Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition limits and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Remaining members shall be appointed by National Committees and National Societies; not more than three members may be chosen to represent a single nation; the Committee may add members as deemed desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments are intended to ensure broad international representation; additional members may be added to reflect diverse interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for committee actions to be operative
rubrics_metrics.description: No action relating to nomenclature shall be considered complete and operative until it has been considered by all members of the Committee, until adequate publicity has been given with respect to actions proposed, until approval has been given by a majority of two thirds of the members of the Committee, and until a report has been made to the next succeeding International Congress for Microbiology with opportunity for objection, modification or rejection by action of the Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes full-member consideration, public notice, supermajority approval (two-thirds), and subsequent reporting to Congress for potential review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee duties: topics to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall consider problems such as criteria to be employed in classification, adoption of names for species and genera conservanda, type species (including their preservation and identification), encouragement of monographing special groups or genera by those best qualified, enlargement/support of type culture collections, and preparation/publication of Committee and Subcommittee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad remit covering classification criteria, conservation of names, types, culture collections, and publication of advisory reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of type/published strains in culture collections
rubrics_metrics.description: All bacteriologists publishing descriptions of new species or important strains of bacteria should deposit pure cultures of such with a culture collection so they may be made available to others interested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges adequate financial support for culture collections by official agencies, institutions, and foundations; treats culture collections as invaluable repositories for taxonomy and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Species Plantarum 1753 as point of departure
rubrics_metrics.description: It is believed that the greatest stability will be conferred by the adoption of the publication of Species Plantarum by Linnaeus in 1753 as the point of departure for bacterial nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical anchoring of priority for bacterial names to the 1753 linnaean starting point; suggestion that no present action be taken immediately regarding a list of genera conservanda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of homonymy (Protista and other groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic homonyms are not permitted in the group Protista; it is advisable to avoid homonymy amongst Protista on the one hand, and plants or animals (Metazoa) on the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to prevent duplication of generic names across related kingdoms/groups to avoid illegitimacy of later homonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of specific epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteriologists should accept Article 13: While specific substantive names derived from names of persons may be written with a capital initial letter, all other specific names are to be written with a small initial letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes capitalization practice for species epithets consistent with zoological rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for drafting a Bacteriological Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The tentative code differed from the Botanical Code principally by reorganization of text under clear headings, elimination of items inapplicable to bacteriology, simplification through rephrasing, and selection of examples from bacteriology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting other codes, tailor structure, remove irrelevant sections, simplify language, and use field-specific examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Committee functions
rubrics_metrics.description: To consider and pass upon all recommendations relating to the formation or modification of Rules of Nomenclature; to consider Opinions rendered by the Judicial Commission; to designate official Type Culture Collections; to receive and act on reports from committees; to hold at least one meeting triennially with the Congress; to report its actions to the final Plenary Session; and to cooperate with other committees (Botanical/Zoological).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the Committee's authority over rules, designation of collections, intercommittee cooperation, reporting, and periodic meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Commission functions — interpretative Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: To issue formal Opinions when asked to interpret rules of nomenclature in cases in which the application of a rule is doubtful; to prepare formal Opinions relative to the status of names, placing such names in special lists (Nomina Conservanda, Nomina Rejicienda, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial Commission serves as authoritative interpreter and can place names into conservation or rejection lists to stabilize nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Commission functions — types, lists, and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare formal Opinions relative to types (particularly types of species and genera) and develop a list of bacterial genera with type species; to prepare and publish lists of names proposed for bacteria/protozoa/other groups to assist authors in avoiding illegitimate homonyms; to develop a list of publications whose names of organisms shall have no standing in bacteriology in determination of priority; to edit and publish the International Rules, Opinions, and Lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive stewardship role including authoritative lists and editorial responsibility for official nomenclatural documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Commission procedural requirements for issuing Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an interpretation of any rule is desirable, a microbiologist should prepare a brief outlining the problem, citing pertinent references and indicating reasons for and against specific interpretations; submit to the Chairman; an Opinion will be formulated which may not be issued until it has been approved by at least eight members of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal submission procedure requiring substantiation and supermajority approval (eight members) before issuing Opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and terms of Judicial Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission consists of twelve members (exclusive of ex officio) serving in three classes of four commissioners each for nine years so that one class retires at every International Congress; ex officio members include the two Permanent Secretaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggered long terms intended to ensure continuity; vacancies filled by the International Committee for unexpired terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative publication and testing of proposed Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Code shall be regarded as wholly tentative, published for testing so that it may be brought up for further consideration and final disposition at the next Microbiological Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages distribution and testing of a tentative code widely before final adoption to solicit comments and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and editorial oversight (Editorial Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Editorial Board was established consisting of the Chairman of the Judicial Commission and the two Permanent Secretaries; publication of a quarterly 'International Bulletin of Bacteriological Nomenclature and Taxonomy' was authorized to be edited by the Editorial Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a formal editorial structure for publishing rules, Opinions, and nomenclatural matters on an ongoing basis.
